verdict.rationale: Fastmail's developer page documents first-party JMAP access: a session resource at api.fastmail.com/jmap/session, standard RFC 8620/8621 specs, and API-token auth. Community users independently confirm working IMAP access and SMTP sending with an SMTP-only app password, so the open-protocol core of the story is delivered. missing for 10: any evidence of standards-based export (e.g., mbox/EML, vCard/iCal export), first-party documentation of IMAP/SMTP settings.

support.subject: As a switcher, my mail stays reachable over open protocols and standard formats — IMAP/JMAP/SMTP access and standards-based export — so no client can lock me in

citations.quote: The JMAP session resource can be found at https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session
JMAP is an open standard any organisation can implement, not more proprietary lock-in from big tech companies.
Uses Fastmail SMTP for transactional emails with an app password that can only access SMTP.
